info.description:
Global markets intelligence for equities, commodities, indices, crypto, and AI, and the people and topics around them. /search turns any text into IDs: assets take `asset_id` with `asset_class` (equity, commodity, index, or crypto); people and topics take `subject_id`. /top-trending shows what the market is talking about now.

Timestamps are UTC RFC 3339. Share fields are fractions from 0 to 1; `_pct` fields are percentage points. Every endpoint is on every plan: Free reads 90 days of history at 60 requests a minute, Pro each endpoint's full history at 300.

Responses carry RateLimit-* headers and, when priced, X-Credits-Charged and X-Credits-Remaining. Errors are JSON with `error` and `message`, and are never charged: 400 invalid request, 401 bad key, 402 out of credits, 403 beyond your plan's history, 404 not found, 429 rate limited (wait Retry-After seconds), 503 briefly unavailable (retry after Retry-After) or too slow (narrow the window).

Send `locale` or `X-Nebula-Locale` for generated text in Spanish, Italian, Turkish, Russian, Korean, Japanese, or Chinese. Server-side only: there are no CORS headers.

get.description:
One cluster's behavioural traits, each ranked against every other cluster (`rank` 1 is the highest):

- `earliness` (days): how early it posts around hype-cycle peaks; positive is early.
- `contrarian` (share): assets where it leans the opposite way to the market.
- `hype_fade` (days): positive means it turns less bullish as hype builds.
- `conviction` (days): how long it holds the same view on an asset.
- `focus` (share): posts on its top 5 assets.
- `breadth` (count): assets it discusses.
- `bullishness` (share): bullish share of its bullish and bearish posts.
- `discovery` (share): posts on assets outside the market's top 100.
- `turnover` (share): how much its top 10 assets change week to week.
- `coverage` (share): hype cycles it took part in.

A hype cycle is a day an asset's posts spike to at least 3× normal. Complete UTC days only.

- Send `cluster_id`.
- `cluster_id` names one cluster; to compare several, call once per cluster or use /clusters for every cluster at once.
- Posting communities (`wallstreetbets`, `reddit`) cover equities only: with one of them, `asset_class` must include `equity`.

get.description:
Rank assets or subjects by one 24-hour measure and filter on the others: share, share change, posts, net bullish posts (bullish minus bearish; negative is bearish), or 24-hour price change. Ranges are inclusive and combine; price filters apply to assets only.

Share is the fraction of all posts in the same market over the same 24 hours (stocks, crypto, or people and topics), bots excluded; with `clusters`, it is the share of what those clusters posted.

Parameter rules:
- `asset_class` applies only to `kind=asset`.
- Posting communities such as `wallstreetbets` are accepted only for `kind=asset` with `asset_class` equity, commodity, or index.
- Each minimum must not exceed its maximum.
- Price sorting and price ranges need `kind=asset`.

parameters.description: What to rank: asset (stocks, commodities, indices, or crypto) or subject (people, accounts, and topics). Defaults to asset.
parameters.name: kind

parameters.description: With kind=asset, the market to rank: equity (the default), commodity, index, or crypto.
parameters.name: asset_class

parameters.description:
Author clusters to read; repeat to combine, for example `clusters=kols&clusters=media`. Selected clusters are added together, and an author can belong to several.
- Callers: `smart_money` (best-performing callers), `dumb_money` (worst-performing), `top_degens` (best on small-cap crypto)
- Timing: `early_movers` (first to talk about an asset as attention rises), `late_movers` (arrive at the peak or after)
- Builders: `developers`, `founders`, `team_leaders`, `project_accounts`
- Institutions: `vcs`, `asset_managers`, `dao_guild_funds`, `incubators`, `exchanges`
- Influence: `kols`, `celebrities`, `media`, `marketer`, `shiller`
- Analysts: `ta_analyst`, `fa_analyst`, `macro_analyst`, `onchain_analyst`, `investigators`
- Traders: `position_trader`, `swing_trader`, `day_trader`
- Bias: `perma_bull`, `doomer`, `tribalist`
- Other: `political`, `nft`, `bots`, `automated_ai`
- Communities, by where the post was made: `wallstreetbets`, `reddit`

get.description:
How bullish or bearish the conversation is about an asset, a subject, or a whole market, over time. `sentiment_signal` is bullish minus bearish posts over the trailing 24 hours, recent posts weighted more: positive is net bullish. It grows with volume, so compare an asset with its own history.

`cohorts` gives the same measure for bots and, for one asset or subject, top callers. Send `clusters` to read one or more author groups, or leave out the asset and subject for a market-wide view.

Parameter rules:
- `asset_id` must be sent with `asset_class`.
- `subject_id` cannot be combined with `asset_id` or `asset_class`.
- Without `asset_id`, `asset_class` must be `equity` or `crypto`; `commodity` and `index` need an `asset_id`.

parameters.description: Asset ID from /assets or /search, such as NVDA, GLD, SPX, or bitcoin. Send it with the asset_class returned alongside it.
parameters.name: asset_id

parameters.description: With asset_id, the asset's class. Without it, the market to aggregate: equity (stocks, commodities, and indices; the default) or crypto.
parameters.name: asset_class

parameters.description: Canonical non-asset identifier returned by /subjects or /search, such as text:jensen huang or handle:elonmusk. Accepted in any case. It cannot be combined with asset_id or asset_class.
parameters.name: subject_id

parameters.description:
Author clusters to read; repeat to combine, for example `clusters=kols&clusters=media`. Selected clusters are added together, and an author can belong to several.
- Callers: `smart_money` (best-performing callers), `dumb_money` (worst-performing), `top_degens` (best on small-cap crypto)
- Timing: `early_movers` (first to talk about an asset as attention rises), `late_movers` (arrive at the peak or after)
- Builders: `developers`, `founders`, `team_leaders`, `project_accounts`
- Institutions: `vcs`, `asset_managers`, `dao_guild_funds`, `incubators`, `exchanges`

- Traders: `position_trader`, `swing_trader`, `day_trader`
- Bias: `perma_bull`, `doomer`, `tribalist`
- Other: `political`, `nft`, `bots`, `automated_ai`
- Communities, by where the post was made: `wallstreetbets`, `reddit`

get.description:
The assets or subjects gaining share of the conversation fastest: this 24 hours' share minus the previous 24 hours'. `share_change_pct` is the same change relative to yesterday's share.

Share is the fraction of all posts in the same market over the same 24 hours (stocks, crypto, or people and topics), bots excluded; with `clusters`, it is the share of what those clusters posted.

Parameter rules:
- `asset_class` applies only to `kind=asset`.
- Posting communities such as `wallstreetbets` are accepted only for `kind=asset` with `asset_class` equity, commodity, or index.

parameters.description: What to rank: asset (stocks, commodities, indices, or crypto) or subject (people, accounts, and topics). Defaults to asset.
parameters.name: kind

parameters.description: With kind=asset, the market to rank: equity (the default), commodity, index, or crypto.
parameters.name: asset_class

parameters.description:
Author clusters to read; repeat to combine, for example `clusters=kols&clusters=media`. Selected clusters are added together, and an author can belong to several.
- Callers: `smart_money` (best-performing callers), `dumb_money` (worst-performing), `top_degens` (best on small-cap crypto)
- Timing: `early_movers` (first to talk about an asset as attention rises), `late_movers` (arrive at the peak or after)
- Builders: `developers`, `founders`, `team_leaders`, `project_accounts`
- Institutions: `vcs`, `asset_managers`, `dao_guild_funds`, `incubators`, `exchanges`
- Influence: `kols`, `celebrities`, `media`, `marketer`, `shiller`
- Analysts: `ta_analyst`, `fa_analyst`, `macro_analyst`, `onchain_analyst`, `investigators`
- Traders: `position_trader`, `swing_trader`, `day_trader`
- Bias: `perma_bull`, `doomer`, `tribalist`
- Other: `political`, `nft`, `bots`, `automated_ai`
- Communities, by where the post was made: `wallstreetbets`, `reddit`
parameters.name: clusters

parameters.description: Maximum results returned.
parameters.name: limit

asset_class.description: The market whose assets were ranked; absent for subjects.

clusters.description: The author clusters whose posts were counted, canonicalised; empty when every author except bots was counted.

from.description: UTC start of the ranked 24 hours. The comparison window is the 24 hours before it.

kind.description: What was ranked: asset or subject, as requested.

previous_total_posts.description: All posts in the ranked population over the previous 24 hours.

asset_class.description: The asset's class: equity (stocks and ETFs), commodity, index, or crypto. Send it with asset_id on every asset-scoped request.

asset_id.description: Canonical public asset identifier: the ticker or market symbol for stocks, commodities, and indices, and the CoinGecko slug (or, without one, a numeric id) for crypto.

kind.description: What the result is: asset (query it with asset_id and asset_class) or subject (query it with subject_id).

posts.description: This result's posts over the ranked 24 hours.

previous_posts.description: This result's posts in the immediately preceding window of equal length.

price_change_24h_pct.description: Raw market-price change over 24 hours, in percentage points.

share.description: This result's posts as a fraction of all posts in the ranked population over the same 24 hours, from 0 to 1.

share_change.description: Change in share against the previous window, as a decimal fraction: 0.01 is one percentage point. Absent only when the population had no posts in the previous window.

share_change_pct.description: The change in share relative to the previous window's share, in percent. Absent when the result had no posts in the previous window.

subject_id.description: Canonical identifier for a non-asset person, account, or topic.

to.description: UTC end of the ranked 24 hours: when the ranking was computed.

total_posts.description: All posts in the ranked population over the 24 hours: the denominator of share.

x-x402.authentication: PAYMENT-SIGNATURE on the separate base path; no API key or account credits. MCP and CLI authentication are unchanged.
x-x402.availability: Disabled by default; requires operator configuration. x-x402-eligible marks compatible operations, not deployment status.
x-x402.pricing: Fixed operation credits multiplied by configured USDC micros per credit. Read the PAYMENT-REQUIRED offer for the deployed price, network and recipient.
x-x402.responses: Query and successful response schemas are shared. HTTP 402 negotiates payment; PAYMENT-RESPONSE carries the settlement receipt. Settlement uncertainty returns 503 and must be reconciled before signing a new payment.
